newsitem.title: JORDAN: U.S. envoy to Mideast meets Jordan's King Hussein.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to Mideast meets Jordan's King Hussein.

text.p: U.S. envoy to the Middle East Dennis Ross briefed Jordan's King Hussein on Monday on his efforts to restart stalled talks between Israel and the Palestinians.
Ross, who met the king after talks with Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, praised Jordan's support for his mediation efforts and said the troubled Middle East peace process was still alive.

"There is no question that Jordan is strongly committed to the peace process and will always be supportive of any effort to try to find ways to put things back on track," Ross told reporters after meeting Majali.

Information Minister Samir Mutawae said Ross highlighted Jordan's mediation role in a January accord under which Israel pulled its troops back from 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron. Jordan, which signed a 1994 peace treaty with Israel, has a large Palestinian population but also forged close ties with Israel.

"(Ross) emphasised the importance of Jordanian diplomacy... and cited the example of the Hebron agreement and wished that Jordan continues its good efforts with both sides, the Palestinians and Israelis," Mutawae said.

Ross is trying to bring together Palestinian and Israeli negotiators to end a two-month freeze in negotiations on expanding Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, occupied by Israel in the 1967 Arab-Israeli war.

Palestinian officials said they will attend a meeting to be held soon with Israelis but said they doubt it will lead to a resumption of the peace talks, halted in March when Israel started work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Ross, who was due to return to Israel on Monday after a lunch with King Hussein, said both sides had shown "the understanding...that there is no acceptable alternative to the peace process".
"What I believe, based on the discussions that I have had... (is) that the peace process is alive," he said.
